meta_thesis: With no balance patch since mid-September, the cast is unusually flat: roughly 60% of heroes sit in one bloated A tier, and the new City Never Sleeps map is doing the work instead. The map favors tempo — comeback mechanics are nerfed so early leads stick, and fights happen in open, less choked, less rooftop-dominated terrain. That means open-space teamfighters, clustered-jungle farmers with AoE lifesteal, and high-mobility heroes (especially ones that can reach the new pickups) move up, while rooftop-reliant or choke-dependent heroes move down.

hero_claims.why: Called the best hero in the game and 'genuinely broken' — tankiest, does damage, has CC, low skill floor, and no ELO where he isn't OP. New stat scaling on armor makes a 5,000 HP hero better for free.

New jungle is clustered so he cleaves camp clusters with his 2 and max-2 procs; hardest carry to invade, hits his spike ~10 minutes early, and ends up an M1 carry with ~4,800 HP. 'If I'm ahead, you lose' character — caveat: needs peel, so solo-Q is worse than the tier suggests.

Gut-read as the S-tier gatekeeper: does well in both full-open and closed fights, the map's verticality suits her, and the new healing bats are on her route. Enhanced Refresher lines up with her ball for permanent double-ball uptime.
Only hero that lets a team rotate smoothly onto the new three-center objectives — 'that has to be valuable'; great CC and damage. Moved from A to S mid-video.
Always OP in high elo: the debuff character that cuts a 3,000 DPS team to 1,400, plus global pressure to shut down side-lane splits. Boring to play against, never bad.
Explicitly bottom of S: in ranked draft, with a counterpick available, one of the most broken heroes in the game; without the right enemy comp he's much lower.

'The new map is so built for Lash' — new Chinatown Tower is his stomping ground, and he has the best access in the game to the new healing bats (10% max HP). S tier for most ELOs regardless of hitbox bugs.
Strong and in need of a rework call-out: multiple charges on her grapple is 'one of the worst decisions ever'. Ranks her S while asking for the mechanic to be deleted next major patch.
Strong but skill-gated — 'you can't spawn in and carry'. Same power as Abrams, slightly better. Not OP; his hook-recast reset should be removed and compensated elsewhere.
Rated above Apollo and the best of the recent hero additions: benefits from open space and the jungle rework, great frontline in open teamfights, and good new-jungle clear. Never a bad pick.
Strong early game and economy — 'very good invades' and the new map's abundance of boxes feeds her gold. Still unclear ceiling because she has no CC and isn't tanky.
Can teleport from the top of the new Chinatown Tower directly onto camps around the map and get out free without going downstairs — a huge invade and tempo play.

The clearest map-winner with no number changes: new terrain has far fewer roofs above flyers, so he is now the high ground instead of dying to M1 carries standing on rooftops. Same build as before; only terrain changed.
Was already good and is slightly buffed now — 'I really like Haze on this patch for invading'. Not S: bad matchups, low HP, needs finesse.
'Objectively never bad' — struggles in the fully open environments but eats the new jungle with heavy melee, so the map shift is a wash rather than a nerf. Placed low A.

Strongest she has been: every clustered jungle camp is a ~1,000 HP heal off her rake — you can kite the new camps and rake everything for ~1,500 — and open teamfights let her ult shine. Strong but balanced.
Promoted from a low tier: valued for the new three-center objectives ('three safe objectives') and team utility. Tier depends on whether the 8-second enhanced Divine Barrier access stays in the game.
Low-key buffed by the map: can swap people out of open areas, notably mid lane, from under the walker with little counterplay. Carbine build still strong — good, not nerf-demanding.

High mobility plus abundant jungle on a map that rewards exactly that — top of A, maybe bottom S. Data point: win rate climbs from ~45% to ~55% with 300 games on the hero, so he's skill-gated, not weak.
The open map lets her chain the heal across everything with no effort, and the new Sinners are a big gold swing she converts well. Also has excess gold for Knockdown to answer picks like Vindicta.
Always good — tanky, does damage, strong lane, mid and late. No rant needed; bruisers are strong on average and he's one of the most impactful if piloted well.
Whatever Shiv is, Silver is — good early, mid and late, but at a pro level he's 'lame' and can be the best hero in the game. Ranked average is lower because positioning is worse.
Solid and consistently good, but the creator can't judge him honestly because he's very strong on the hero himself; one-tricks get A-tier value while others get zero.
In high elo Viper has always had a very high win rate and is stronger than most people think; low-elo performance unknown.
Called good and placed in A, explicitly rated above Infernus. Contrasted against Warden, whom he calls weak.
Top of B and the archetype of a healthy hero: solid, not OP, and the most balanced hero in the game. Slightly worse than last patch but does not need buffs or nerfs.

Better than people think: with comeback mechanics nerfed, his early-duelist kit snowballs, and the new Repost plus its range annoys the common strong picks (Lash, Mina). On-screen board still places him in B and he was never moved despite the narration — treat the placement as soft.

Top of B and balanced — the new terrain suits him and he doesn't need a buff or nerf. Ceiling capped because blind-picking him into a Sinclair counterpick is griefing, and he forces his carries to build differently.
Balanced in the plainest sense: not OP, not bad, nothing wrong with the kit — 'playable but on the lower tier'.

Solid and correctly tuned — needs neither buffs nor nerfs. Caveat: the enhanced Divine Barrier on an 8-second cooldown seen on multiple players per game would nullify him, and that access is described as temporary.

Top B / maybe bottom A: 'will always be strong' because the ult is on such a short cooldown, giving built-in map control like Mirage. Good paired with the strong gun heroes; worse at support than Rem or Paige.
Not unplayable but clearly outclassed — 'I would way rather have a Rem or a Paige than a Kelvin'. Carry Kelvin is a one-game novelty, not optimal.

Weakest of the interchangeable gun carries: countered by the top-of-list heroes and structurally hurt because early game now matters more and comeback mechanics were nerfed, killing his lose-lane/AFK-farm pattern. Why play him when Venator lanes and closes better?
A chud: possibly fine in low elo with the new jungle, but outclassed by gun carries like Venator who are stronger all game and don't fall off. Not unplayable, not strong.

Top of B: the map buffs her, but Grey Talon does the job better and many of her counters (Mo & Krill ult, Rem with Knockdown, Yamato, Bebop, Apollo Repost) are meta. 'Do not play Vin, you will lose' in solo Q; fine in a duo.
Feels weak and outclassed by heroes doing the same job better; framed as needing minor buffs. Better than Seven, but not rated highly.
The open map is bad for him — 'I do not want to be a Graves in the full open' — and he can't full solo-carry a game like an M1 hero. Playable with moments, but not preferable.

Her wall is devalued because the new map has fewer chokes and can simply be walked around; the old instant-cutoff wall on a retreating target doesn't exist anymore. Not useless, just junk relative to options.

item_claims.why: On Celeste it lines up with her ball, giving permanent double-ball uptime in the late game — one of the enhanced items he calls 'turbo cancer'.

An enhanced Divine Barrier on an ~8-second cooldown shows up on two players per game and completely nullifies Infernus; the tier of heroes that grant it depends on whether that access stays, so treat this as low confidence.
Rem has excess gold and buys it specifically to answer flying picks like Vindicta.
Paradox's Carbine build is 'still strong' and keeps her a good pick without being nerf-worthy.
He credits 'the curses' with helping Grey Talon in close-quarters fights against the meta heroes, not just in open terrain — retain low confidence, it may be shorthand for his own kit.

map_claims.claim: The new map is far more open with fewer chokes and, critically, fewer roofs sitting above flyers — on the old map any M1 carry gained high ground over a flyer just by existing, which is no longer true.
Three new center/safe objectives exist (described as 'three centers in the tower'), and the hero who can rotate a team onto all three smoothly (The Doorman for CC, Paige for safety) gains real value.
There are healing bats in the sky that heal 10% of max HP; Celeste and especially Lash have the best access to them and almost nobody is using them yet.

New jungle camps are clustered, so AoE clear and lifesteal-style heals are multiplied: Venator cleaves clusters with his 2, Rem chains her heal across them effortlessly, and Mina can kite camps together and rake them for far more healing than intended.
map_claims.numbers: ~1,000 HP heal per camp for Mina; ~1,500 from a multi-camp rake; 'three times more than it should'

map_claims.claim: Comeback mechanics were nerfed, so early snowballing now has real meaning and lane-phase strength matters more — this is the single biggest systemic shift in the patch.
The new Sinners are a large gold swing that a hero like Rem converts efficiently, adding to the map's tempo bias.
Stat-based armor and magic resist scale with farm — on high-HP farmers like Mo & Krill and Venator, farming safes yields small but real free resistances.
map_claims.numbers: ~3% each armor additional per claim; up to ~6% spirit armor seen free; 5,000 HP late-game heroes; 12 safes farmed per game

map_claims.claim: Boxes/crates are abundant, boosting box-clearing economy heroes like Calico, and heavy melee gives jungle value to heroes like Lady Geist.
The new Chinatown Tower is a power position: Lash's stomping ground, and Drifter can teleport from its top onto surrounding camps and escape for free without descending.

reasoning_patterns: Reads a terrain change as a hero buff with no number change: because the new map has fewer roofs above flyers, Grey Talon is now the high ground instead of free food for M1 carries on rooftops — same build, 'gigabuffed' value.
Treats a system change as a hero-specific buff/nerf pair: nerfed comeback mechanics make early duelists like Apollo stronger and delete Seven's lose-lane/AFK-farm win condition.
Converts a PvE layout change into combat math: clustered jungle plus AoE lifesteal means Mina's rake and Rem's chain heal become free survivability, so a farm-route change is really a sustain change.
Rates by opportunity cost rather than absolute power: Kelvin isn't bad, he's worse than 'a Rem or a Paige', so he falls — same logic applied to Seven, Victor and Vindicta.
Uses data shape over headline number: Pocket's win rate rising ~45% to ~55% with 300 games means a skill-gated hero that 'would have been nerfed months ago' if everyone played him well.
Uses the absence of a balance patch as the explanation for an inflated A tier: most of the cast is playable, so tiering here is about map fit, not power changes.

patch_calls.headline: New map, no balance pass: A tier is bloated because the terrain, not the numbers, decides who wins — and the terrain favors tempo, open-space fighting and clustered-jungle farmers.
non_obvious_calls: Grey Talon is a top map winner with zero kit changes — the removal of rooftops above flyers flips his worst matchup class.
Mina's rake healing off the new clustered jungle camps (~1,000-1,500 HP) is arguably an unintended power spike, and she's the strongest she's ever been without being game-breaking.
Mo & Krill and Venator quietly gain free armor and spirit armor from stat scaling because they farm the most safes on 5,000 HP bodies.
Drifter's ability to teleport from the new Chinatown Tower roof straight onto outlying camps and leave for free is a top-tier invade route nobody is using yet.
The healing bats in the sky (36 of them, 10% max HP) are unclaimed value, and access to them pushes Lash and Celeste up.
Celeste's ceiling is tied to enhanced-item timing: Enhanced Refresher keeps double ball permanently, which is a late-game item interaction rather than a kit change.
The enhanced Divine Barrier on an ~8-second cooldown appearing on two players per game is treated as a temporary distortion that would otherwise bury Infernus.
